title: Enzyme‐assisted purification and characterization of proteins from Chilean granado beans
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

High-purity protein isolates from leguminous crops may contain peptides with enhanced bioactivity and functionality. This study developed a purification strategy to recover protein isolates from Chilean granado beans (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) using targeted enzymatic hydrolysis and ultrafiltration. Two protein fractions – acid-soluble protein isolate (SPI) and precipitated protein isolate (PPI) – were purified by selectively removing carbohydrate and phosphorus-containing impurities using enzymes. Enzymatic treatments with cellulases (CTec3), hemicellulases (HTec3), amylase, and phosphatase were applied at upstream, midstream, and downstream stages of the protein isolates' production process, to evaluate the impact of each enzyme treatment on protein purity.

RESULTS

Treatment with CTec3 and HTec3 enzymes (1.5 g kg−1 substrate and 50 °C) was most effective, increasing PPI and SPI protein concentrations from 805 to 850 g kg−1 and 459 to 911 g kg−1, suggesting better enzyme access after the initial recovery of the proteins. Phosphatase treatment enhanced purity by hydrolyzing phytate-bound phosphorus, while diafiltration facilitated removal of low-molecular-weight solutes in the permeate. Mass balance analysis confirmed phosphorus reductions of 79% in PPI and 62% in SPI, using a 6:1 diafiltration ratio to enhance removal of soluble species.

CONCLUSION

Enzymatic hydrolysis combined with membrane separation enhances the purity of legume-derived protein isolates. Protein recoveries of approximately 76% and 91% for PPI and approximately 100% and 78% for SPI were observed when treated with CTec3 + HTec3, and phosphatase enzymes respectively. These findings provide valuable insights into processes to produce high-purity protein ingredients for food and nutraceutical applications where isolate purity and functionality are critical. © 2026 The Author(s).
